searchText: In theory, lots of zeros can compress well. I have never been a fan of that rule personally though. 0 is just empty byte, it represents `empty` here's the way how I am getting rid of zeros in my contracts ```c++ object "Contract" { code { datacopy(0, dataoffset("runtime"), datasize("runtime")) return(0, datasize("runtime")) } object "runtime" { code { if iszero(eq(0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001111, caller())) { revert(0, 0) } // checks if called by owner switch shr(0xf8, calldataload(0)) // call switch statement on 1 byte function selector case 0 { // selector 0x00 mstore(0, decodeAsUint112(0x01)) return(0, 0x20) // return mem-data from 0 to 32 bytes } case 1 { // selector 0x01 mstore(0, "Hello, World") // store 32 bytes padded hex-encoded `Hello, World` in memory return(0, 0x20) // return mem-data from 0 to 32 bytes } default { revert(0, 0) } // revert if calldata is 0x function decodeAsUint112(_pos) -> v { // 2^112-1, 14 bytes v := shr(sub(0x100, mul(8, sub(calldatasize(), _pos))), calldataload(_pos)) } } } } ``` calldata `0x` will revert calldata `0x002a` will return 32 bytes padded `2a` calldata `0x00ffffffffffffffffffffffffffff` will return 32 bytes padded `ffffffffffffffffffffffffffff` calldata `0x01` will return 32 bytes padded hex-encoded `Hello, World` you can parse any calldata by using `Yul` or by using inline assembly in `Solidity`, you can find more info about it here: https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/develop/yul.html thank you so much everybody, especially for the code example <@!871765808748056606> . I will have to learn some more Solidity to understand what is going on here, but I will! Another question: The gas limit in a block is currently 30 million. In theory, could I publish a single transaction that contains around `30 million * 68 non-zero bytes ≈ 2 GB` of data? And in practice, what would hold be back (despite the cost!)? An unlikeliness for my tx to get mined into a single block? What is perhaps a more realistic tx size limit? assert(gas_price*gas_limit < 10^18) but I am not sure 30,000,000 divided by 68, not times. Divided by 16, not 68 well, technically you could do 30000000/4 if all the bytes are zero bytes but that's pointless and would get compressed down to nothing at network layer anyway 30000000 / 15.953125 for random data, strictly speaking 🤣 😂😂😂 oh... right. ok then it is about 1.8 MB could that be considered a limit for transaction inputs containing only non-zero bytes? 🤔 I have a contract A with ` mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) private balances;` and I want to init another contract B (clone of A) with the same mapping with the values from A, how would you do so? Trying to migrate staking balances from A to B Can anyone suggest any good resources for learning the technicals of zkproofs and their application to blockchain?
